crossRefs.note: Or have only Barnabas and I no right to not work?
What soldier ever serves at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard, and doesn’t eat of its fruit? Or who feeds a flock…
even as I also please all men in all things, not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, that they may be…
For we don’t preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake,
Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of…
For what is there in which you were made inferior to the rest of the assemblies, unless it is that I myself was not a…
nor seeking glory from men (neither from you nor from others), when we might have claimed authority as apostles of…
neither did we eat bread from anyone’s hand without paying for it, but in labor and travail worked night and day, that…
not because we don’t have the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, that you should imitate us.
and those who use the world, as not using it to the fullest. For the mode of this world passes away.
But be careful that by no means does this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
Yet if because of food your brother is grieved, you walk no longer in love. Don’t destroy with your food him for whom…

translations.web: What then is my reward? That when I preach the Good News, I may present the Good News of Christ without charge, so as not to abuse my authority in the Good News.
translations.bsb: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.
translations.kjv: What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.
translations.asv: What then is my reward? That, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel without charge, so as not to use to the full my right in the gospel.
